blocks.text: Npro - C - Erns - E1 - E2 - p7 - NS2 - NS3 - NS4A - NS4B - NS5A - NS5B

blocks.html: Npro and Erns have no counterpart in Hepaciviridae or Pegivirus. Npro is a self-cleaving cysteine autoprotease found nowhere else in the order; Erns is a ribonuclease envelope glycoprotein. That is why Pegivirus, which has neither and no capsid at all, is a separate module rather than a genus in this one.

The dump excludes records under 1,000 nt — 29,157 of 33,605. The median pestivirus record is 248 nt, shorter even than Hepacivirus's 467-nt NS5B fragment, and cannot yield a protein above any runt floor. It changes the denominator of every ‘% binned’ figure here.

sections.lede: One genus, one polyprotein, cut into twelve products plus the polyprotein itself. ICTV split the old Flaviviridae in 2025; BV-BRC still files every pestivirus under family = Flaviviridae, and the module name follows ICTV.

blocks.html: The string carrying the parenthetical (NS3) is the one that is not NS3. Both appear on nearly every genome. 896 precursors were routed out of NS3 by length; before routing its median was 1,136 aa, after it is 683.

sections.lede: Binning on wording would have put 2,390 precursors into two features. Both were caught by measuring length against the reference, not by reading the string.

sections.title: Does it route?

blocks.html: NS2 is the feature with no training data, and it calls on 111 genomes. That is 69.8% overall and 86% of the genomes where both its anchors exist — it can only be cut where p7 and NS3 are both called, and p7 is 81.1%.

E2, p7, Npro and NS5A read low for one reason and it is not the profiles. The failures are whole-species and all-or-nothing — every genome of Pestivirus scrofae, ferret, bamboo rat, Norway rat and pangolin pestivirus fails, or none does. Of the taxa missing E2, none has a single E2 training sequence; for p7, none; for NS5A, 19 of 21 have none. BV-BRC annotates the polyprotein for the atypical pestiviruses and does not cut it.

sections.lede: 172 genomes annotated, species-capped across 60 species. 159 routed; 13 called nothing.
sections.title: Does it call the proteins?

blocks.html: BV-BRC holds 69 records under a pestivirus NS2 string. Only 34 are NS2-length, and 24 of those 34 do not end in the right residue. Pestivirus mostly does not cleave NS2-3 — uncleaved NS2-3 is the normal product of non-cytopathic BVDV — and the CSFV reference NC_002657 annotates no NS2 at all.

So NS2 is not modelled. It is cut from p7's C-terminus to the residue before NS3's N-terminal Gly. That Gly is the Gly1590 of the conserved Arg1589-Gly1590 site, established by protein sequencing of two cytopathic BVDV strains (Tautz & Thiel, Arch Virol 2003, PMID 12827468). The motif R|GPAVC is present in 358 of 400 pestivirus polyproteins, and 534 of 556 NS3 records begin GPAVCK.

The same method was tried on Npro and rejected. Cys168-Ser169 is equally well established (Rumenapf 1998 PMID 9499122; Gottipati 2013 PMID 24146623), but derivation gave no coverage gain (120 calls against the PSSM's 122) and the C-terminus collapsed from 96% ending in the conserved Cys168 to 58%. A derived end inherits whatever boundary its anchor places, and only 43 of 100 shared genomes agreed. NS2 works because its anchor is the literature site; Npro's anchor is the capsid profile, which does not place that junction reliably. Npro keeps its PSSMs.

sections.lede: The change of method, and the one number that shows it worked.
sections.title: NS2, cut at a site fixed by protein sequencing

blocks.html: Mature peptides in the atypical pestiviruses. E2, p7 and NS5A go uncalled in 16-21 lineages that have no training sequence for those features. Derivation is the route, and it is available for E2 (anchored on E1 and p7) but not for p7: p7 would need E2 and NS2 as anchors, and NS2 is itself derived — the machinery anchors only on PSSM matches, not on other derived features. That is a real limit of the mechanism, not an oversight.
13 of 172 genomes call nothing at all, and 28.9% are genuinely clean. The panel is species-capped, so it gives every one of 60 species equal weight and deliberately over-weights the divergent tail.

standfirst: Bovine viral diarrhea, classical swine fever and border disease, plus a growing tail of atypical pestiviruses from rodents, bats, ferrets and pangolins. Thirteen features over one polyprotein — and one of them, NS2, is not modelled from the database at all. It is cut at a cleavage site fixed by protein sequencing, because the database's own NS2 records are too few and too wrong to train on.
